html:
The Zondo Commission was a judicial inquiry into state capture in South Africa, led by Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo, which held hearings from 2018 and delivered its final reports in 2022.

It examined claims that during the presidency of Jacob Zuma, from 2009 to 2018, the Gupta family and others had won control over ministers, state companies such as the power utility Eskom, and contracts worth billions. Witnesses described bribes, rigged tenders and looted funds.

Zuma refused to testify and was jailed for contempt of court in 2021, which set off deadly riots and looting in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng. The reports named many officials, though few have been convicted. The inquiry showed how corruption had weakened the state built after 1994 by the ANC in South Africa.
sum: The Zondo Commission was a judicial inquiry into state capture in South Africa, led by Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo, which held hearings from 2018 and delivered its final reports in 2022.
